title: Choose the visual world for Steel City Codes // Denver
question: The roll assigned Camp Shirt. Keep it, take Terminal Yellow, or re-roll. Both keep the wordmark and brand gold; the sketches show the parent home screen on a phone.

options.label: Camp Shirt
options.lineage: screenprinted summer-camp staff tees and tour-shirt back prints
options.thesis: Four flat spot inks, each with one job, on a white page: the camp's own shirt, worn by the software.
materials: flat spot ink, no shadows or gradients
heavy ink rules instead of cards
options.viewport: Ink bar with wordmark and top tabs; each camper is a ruled block with one status ink and a back-print row for their week.
options.risk: Can read stark if the ink rules are too heavy or the white page goes unbroken on long admin tables.

raised.raise: One ply only: content never floats; only the inline edit layer lifts.
Every camper, volunteer and applicant row carries the same fixed furniture in the same order: name, age or role, safety flag, status.
In schedules, a block's height is its duration, so a 3-hour class reads three times a 1-hour duty.
Section codes (WEB-1, PY-B) and week numbers are the stable identifiers, set identically on every screen.
Hierarchy comes from type scale and ink weight, not boxes; a container appears only where a group needs a boundary.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.lineage: international airport wayfinding (yellow overhead sign bands)
options.thesis: Every screen is a junction sign: only the next decision, with room number and time at monumental scale.
materials: yellow sign panels with ink type
options.viewport: A gold sign band leads with the next thing to do (Room 202, Monday 9:00), then a list of decisions per camper.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity (one next decision, no dead ends), but loses on identification: gold everywhere spends the brand colour on panels and fights the 'gold is for emphasis' rule.
options.risk: Big yellow bands on every screen turn admin tables into a sign wall and leave gold no power for the primary button.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with tab dividers
options.thesis: Sections as coloured divider boards under clear acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the edge, the current section's board behind the content.
options.case: Parents and teen volunteers don't know this object, and a tab rail fights top tabs on phones.
options.risk: Costume of a manual on a working screen.
options.kept: One ply only: a single elevation rule.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Every camper as a mascot cell with fixed personal furniture.
options.viewport: A ranked grid of rounded cells.
options.case: Ranking kids is wrong for this product and pastels repeat the incumbent's confetti.
options.kept: Fixed furniture in a fixed order on every person row.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Time as a vertical staff where length is duration.
options.case: Nobody here reads notation; upward time confuses a daily schedule.
options.kept: Block height equals duration in schedules.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.thesis: Every entity gets a catalogue number; colour codes replace words.
options.viewport: A black index of numbered entries.
options.case: Coded labels hide meaning from parents in a hurry.
options.risk: Mystery where clarity is the job.
options.kept: Stable identifiers (WEB-1, Week 1) set the same way everywhere.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.viewport: One giant glyph with a grid below.
options.case: No task here is about letterforms.
options.kept: Type scale and weight carry hierarchy instead of boxes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean school-registration app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement parents expect from school portals, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other camp sign-up by design.
